subject.title: fix(proxy): redact sensitive headers in standalone debug proxy captures

question: Should standalone captures adopt the runtime's broad name-and-fragment redaction policy, accepting that non-secret headers such as `access-control-allow-credentials` will also be masked?
rationale: Sharing the existing classifier closes the secret-persistence gap, but the broader diagnostic information loss is intentional compatibility behavior rather than a correctness question automation can settle.

options.title: Accept shared redaction
options.body: Land the shared policy after exact-head checks, accepting broad masking as the safer default for diagnostic captures.

options.title: Narrow the classifier first
options.body: Define a more precise sensitive-header contract and update both runtime and standalone tests before merging.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep standalone captures unchanged until maintainers define whether operators may retain complete sensitive-header diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Accept shared redaction
recommendation.body: Land the shared policy after exact-head checks, accepting broad masking as the safer default for diagnostic captures.

likelyOwner.reason: The proxy-capture feature originated in their merged work, making them the strongest available owner for its diagnostic-versus-secrecy contract.
